text.p: Indonesian polyster manufacturer PT Polysindo Eka Perkasa on Monday announced a US$800 million expansion programme which will take its production capacity of purified terephthalic acid to 500,000 tonnes per annum from the current 340,000 tonnes.

The company, the flagship of the Texmaco Group, said in a statement that polymer production capacity will rise to 500,000 tonnes per annum from the current 300,000 tonnes after the five-year expansion programme, expected to be completed by 2001.
The expansion will be financed by internally generated funds and additional equity and debt, depending on market conditions, the company said.
"Vertical integration has been the cornerstone of Polysindo's growth strategy to date," president director Marimutu Sinivasan said in the statement.
"Vertical integration has also protected our profitability margins through fluctuations in the pricing cycle."
Other facets of the expansion programme include building new yarn facilities to increase production to 210,000 tonnes per annum from the current 65,000 tonnes, Polysindo said.
Polysindo will also launch production of 25 million yards per annum of polyster fleece and coated active wear fabric under the programme, the statement said.
